name: Tony G. Chen
title: Assistant Professor; Mechanical Intelligence Robotics Lab PI
department: George W. Woodruff School of Mechanical Engineering
fitReason: Moderate, hardware-centered fit: one current published system integrates learned visual detection with actual aerial perching, while the main lab focus is mechanical design rather than RL or foundation-model algorithms.

physicalEvidence.summary: January 1, 2026 SLAP full paper verifies a PercepTree-based CNN tree detector feeding a polynomial planner on a physical 1.2 kg Uvify IFO-S drone. Indoor Stanford experiments use motion-capture localization, offboard Orin processing and human verification before perching; 20 trials evaluate the full detection-to-perch system. Learned bark/species classification is explicitly not implemented, and flight control is not learned. The paper states Chen was at Stanford when the work was performed, so this is prior-institution collaborative hardware, not verified current GT flight-lab access.

shortVisit.summary: Current GT faculty profile and MIRL homepage/people page verify PI appointment and a current team, including graduate advisees. No current external-master’s short-visit invitation or summer-2027 opening was verified.
